quality_checks: The final user-facing deliverable is one self-contained HTML file named agent-codebase-analysis/agent-architecture-analysis.html.
inventory.json, if produced, is internal scratch under .analysis-work and is not presented as a user-facing output.
The skill does not produce evidence-map.html, design-report.md, key-mechanisms.md, or architecture-visuals.md as primary deliverables.
The HTML report combines executive summary, design analysis, key mechanisms, diagrams, evidence citations, reading path, and verification checks.

Mermaid diagrams are mandatory and embedded in the same HTML. The report includes at least system boundary, request lifecycle, harness state machine, context/memory flow, tool/action/RAG flow, and multi-agent topology or control-plane/execution-plane split when applicable.
Each Mermaid diagram has a plain-language explanation and evidence citations.
Each Mermaid/SVG diagram has a visible zoom/open-larger interaction, and overly complex diagrams are split rather than rendered with tiny text.
If compiled SVG is unavailable, the HTML includes renderable Mermaid source blocks and Mermaid initialization rather than omitting diagrams.
Mechanisms are explained in plain language before code citations; class names and function names are used only as evidence, not as the explanation itself.
Each major section uses three layers: newcomer-friendly explanation, architecture details, and representative code evidence.
The table of contents includes a terminology glossary section when English-only or project-native terms may confuse newcomers.
When the glossary exists, the table of contents includes a visible anchor link to it, preferably #terminology-glossary.
Glossary term selection considers general architecture terms, project-native concepts, English-only phrases, and interview-frequency agent design terms that are relevant to the project.
The report starts from the system task boundary: user job, input, output, success condition, and dominant complexity.
The report treats the harness as the core object and explains runtime loop, state machine, context management, tool execution, model abstraction, permissions, persistence/replay, and observability.
For single-agent systems, the report explains long-task progress: goal/plan formation, task workbench, error recovery, context budget, and completion checks.

For multi-agent systems, the report explains topology, responsibility boundaries, shared versus isolated state, communication protocol, merge/verification, termination, permission model, and coordination cost.
RAG/knowledge, if present, is explained as a project-specific pipeline from ingestion through retrieval, ranking, context insertion, citations, update, and evaluation.
Project-native concepts and instruction/memory files such as SOUL.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, MEMORY.md, or PROFILE.md are explained when present.
Important sections include interview-ready explanation callouts that teach how to explain the architecture clearly.
The report cites representative files/functions/classes as evidence for design claims without cataloging every file.
The output avoids byte counts, extension histograms, raw file inventories, exhaustive function lists, per-line code explanations, and implementation recreation checklists.
